full_text_en:
Cui Wenrui — Case of Illegal Speculation and Profiteering

Defendant: Cui Wenrui, male, 51 years old, formerly a retired worker of the Supply and Marketing Cooperative of Suqiao Town, Wen'an County, Hebei Province. Arrested on May 10, 1994.

The case of defendant Cui Wenrui for illegal speculation and profiteering was initiated by the Tianjin Municipal People's Procuratorate Branch to the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court. After public trial, the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court found the following facts:

In April 1993, defendant Cui Wenrui conspired with Shen Huilan and Cao Peizeng (both already sentenced) to engage in illegally issuing and fraudulently issuing invoices for others for the purpose of seeking illegal profits. Thereafter, through the introduction of Cao Peizeng, Cui Wenrui and Shen Huilan negotiated with Yao Yuqiao (already sentenced), manager of Tianjin Yitong Industrial Co., Ltd., to provide invoices to Cui Wenrui and others under the guise of establishing a non-independent accounting unit subordinate to Yitong Industrial Co., Ltd., named "Tianjin Yitong Industrial Co., Ltd. Hardware and Plumbing Purchasing and Sales Department." Subsequently, Cui Wenrui and others also obtained invoices through Li Guo'an (dealt with separately), manager of Tianjin Anda Industrial Co., Ltd.; Fang Guoquan (dealt with separately), manager of Tianjin Beichen District Hardware and Native Produce Business Department; and Zhao Jinru (already sentenced), a cadre of the Civil Affairs Section of Qinghe Street Office, Heping District, Tianjin.

From April 1993 to March 1994, defendant Cui Wenrui, together with Shen Huilan and others, successively issued or fraudulently issued a total of 148 volumes of various invoices, issuing 5,939 copies of invoices with a total invoiced amount of over RMB 13,241,994. Among these, 115 volumes were ordinary invoices, with an invoiced amount of over RMB 10,028,911; 33 volumes were special value-added tax (VAT) invoices, totaling 1,373 copies, with an invoiced amount of over RMB 3,213,083. The illegal profit obtained was over RMB 348,003, with defendant Cui Wenrui and Shen Huilan receiving over RMB 244,603 in illicit proceeds, causing a loss of nearly RMB 1.5 million in state tax revenue. After the incident, RMB 155,660 in illegal gains and some stolen goods were recovered.

The above facts are confirmed by witness testimony, documentary evidence including original invoices, forensic science and technology appraisal conclusions, and confessions of co-defendants, and the defendant also confessed to the facts.

The Tianjin Intermediate People's Court held that, pursuant to Article 2 of the "Provisions on the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Involving the Forgery, Sale, and Theft of Invoices" (see Gazette Issue No. 3, 1994) jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate, which stipulates: "Whoever, for the purpose of profit, illegally issues invoices for others or fraudulently issues invoices for others with an accumulated invoiced amount of RMB 50,000 or more, or illegally issues or fraudulently issues special VAT invoices for others with a deductible tax amount of RMB 10,000 or more, shall be investigated for criminal liability for the crime of illegal speculation and profiteering," Cui Wenrui's conduct constituted the crime of illegal speculation and profiteering. In accordance with Item (1) of Article 1 of the "Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Severely Punishing Criminals Who Seriously Undermine the Economy," severe punishment should be imposed. In accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, all property illegally obtained by the criminal shall be recovered. In accordance with Paragraph 1 of Article 53 of the Criminal Law, Cui Wenrui shall be deprived of political rights for life. Accordingly, on October 6, 1994, the court rendered the following judgment:

1. Defendant Cui Wenrui is guilty of the crime of illegal speculation and profiteering and is sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life;
2. The illegal gains and stolen goods obtained by defendant Cui Wenrui shall be recovered.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, defendant Cui Wenrui appealed to the Tianjin High People's Court, arguing that he did not devise the scheme or gather accomplices in the crime.

The Tianjin High People's Court, upon trial, held that the facts that the appellant, Cui Wenrui, devised schemes, managed finances, and took the lead in dividing the spoils in the criminal activities were supported by the confessions of co-defendants; Cui Wenrui had repeatedly confessed to these facts during pretrial interrogation and the first-instance trial, which was sufficient for determination. His grounds for appeal were untenable. The facts found in the original trial were clear, the evidence was conclusive, the conviction was accurate, the sentence was appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful. Accordingly, on October 17, 1994, the Tianjin High People's Court rendered a ruling pursuant to Item (1) of Article 136 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China: to dismiss the appeal of appellant Cui Wenrui and affirm the original judgment.

Pursuant to Article 144 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the Tianjin High People's Court submitted the case to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

The Supreme People's Court reviewed the case and, on October 24, 1994, rendered a ruling: to approve the criminal ruling of the Tianjin High People's Court affirming the judgment of the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court that defendant Cui Wenrui was guilty of the crime of illegal speculation and profiteering and sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life.
